title: Advanced Topic Modeling Techniques for Categorizing Software Vulnerabilities
subcategory: cybersecurity: comparison of embedding-based and LLM topic models
problem: Large volumes of unstructured vulnerability descriptions are hard to analyse and prioritise manually.
architecture: Comparative pipeline: four BERTopic configurations (UMAP+HDBSCAN, PCA+HDBSCAN, UMAP+DBSCAN, and SentenceTransformer + stacked RoBERTa/GloVe embeddings), CombinedTM (all-mpnet-base-v2 + BoW, 20 topics), Top2Vec, Llama2 with BERTopic for topic labelling, and Mixtral 8x7B prompted to assign five topics per document.
metrics: qualitative inspection (topic similarity heatmaps, hierarchical clustering, word clouds)
baselines: comparison among the listed topic models
key_results: No quantitative coherence or clustering scores are reported; results are presented as similarity matrices, dendrograms and keyword lists.
strengths: Side-by-side use of clustering-based, neural and LLM-based topic modelling on a large industrial security dataset.

limitations.text: Comparison is qualitative only; claims of improved coherence are not supported by reported metric values.
Future work needed for real-time processing and multilingual data.

notes: Application study from the author-curated corpus.
